title: Gunosy says a third party used a business account's credentials to reach its cloud environment and business tools
date_note: Security NEXT published on 2026-11-20 and gives no date for the company's announcement; Gunosy says it detected the activity on 21 October 2026 and reported it to the Personal Information Protection Commission on 23 October.
summary: According to Gunosy, a third party obtained the credentials of a business account by unspecified means and accessed the cloud environment and business tools used to run its service. Part of the emails in that account's mailbox were viewed, and user information registered in the business tools was obtained. Gunosy says 25 business-partner contacts and 107 executives, employees and former employees are affected.
plain: Gunosy says someone used a business account's login details to get into its cloud and work tools. Names and email addresses of 25 business contacts and 107 current and former staff were affected.
exec: Stolen account credentials gave access to cloud systems and mailbox contents; Gunosy reported it to Japan's data protection regulator.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Affected people were notified by email, according to Gunosy; others should protect business accounts with unique credentials and multi-factor sign-in.
impact: Names, email addresses, company names, affiliations, job titles and contact details of 25 business-partner contacts and 107 executives, employees and former employees.

validation.note: Security NEXT (Japan) relaying Gunosy's own statement; Gunosy's notice itself was not read.

review.note: Compared credential use, cloud and tools, mailbox, 21 Oct detection, 23 Oct PPC report, 25 and 107 figures, email notice against Security NEXT 20 Nov 2026
